title: Touring the Dakotas, Black Hills and West with Kid Carter
summary: Riding by car on short jumps through the Black Hills, Bismarck, Colorado and Utah, he sees Custer's monument, the Grand Canyon and Indian girls.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I remember a time when I got to South Dakota, the Black Hills of South Dakota. And we got to a place where they had this statue of Custer's Last Stand. Boy, I thought I was seeing the most important thing that ever happened in history. I didn't know that Custer was such a dolt, trying to go out there and fight them Indians, the way they fight.

But you know, I studied history... Oh. In school, I was a good basketball player. So our coach... My coach was a history teacher, so I was crazy about history. I studied history. I kept up with them grades in history. And that meant... When I got out in North Dakota nad got in them Black Hills...that's in South Dakota... We traveled all around, in Bismarck... And we even traveled all the way out to Colorado. I don't know how Kid Carter got them dates. But when we got...
You were riding in a car, huh?
Yeah. And then I remember gravel roads. That...
It would take you two or three days to get to them places.

Well, he'd line up one town after another. I guess he had some kind of map. He would line up one town... The jumps wasn't over 25 or 100 miles. We didn't have no long jumps. But I remember, we went all the way out to some place in Utah... I know we went... I saw the Grand Canyon early in my life. We just drove by it, and you looked... We just drove on a road where you could look over and look down and see it. And then the colors were so beautiful. And I met those Indians... The prettiest women out there was those Indian girls mixed with White and Indian. They were beautiful. Had the prettiest... And we had a couple of girls in our school that was part-Indian. And they was beautiful. They had beautiful hair...

One of my great friends that lives in New York, Rockmore, he's part-Indian. I don't know whether Rockmore... I think Rockmore had a little land... Because we had a couple of kids in the school that come from them (?) people, you know, that had a little money. Because if you was an Indian or part-Indian, and if you were just born in Oklahoma, you got land. And I always think, boy, what would have happened to me if I had been born a month and ten days... I always say I was born a month and ten days late, because that's how I missed... But it didn't affect me. The one thing it put in my mind was study and get some kind of
knowledge in your mind, so you would be able to make a living. That always stuck with me. So...
